target_claim_or_section: §3 Minimum viable entry point: paid migration assessment + reconciliation report sold to sponsors in a re-platforming window
challenge: At G1 Unbound has no licensed platform for the sponsor to migrate into. G2 is 12-36 months out. So the 'assessment' either sizes a move to a platform that does not exist yet (the buyer cannot act on it inside its contract-end window) or sizes a move to a competitor (Foundant/NPact/Ren), whose own conversion team will redo the mapping under its own SOW. In conversions the receiving vendor owns the conversion programs and the risk, and buyers do not pay a third party for a mapping the receiving vendor will discard. The buyer and the deliverable are both undefined.
evidence: 16 §2 table: G1 4-12 months, G2 licensed platform 12-36 months; 13 §7 ReadinessReport is keyed to adapter_id and Unbound canonical mapping; core conversion practice: the new vendor writes or reuses the conversion program (trackD-techniques row 'Reusable conversion program per source system'; SafeAmerica/Corelation).
proposed_change: Name the buyer and the target platform for each G1 sale. Either (a) reframe G1 as a vendor-neutral 'exit readiness and extraction' service (extraction plan, history inventory, control totals) with no Unbound target mapping, or (b) treat the assessment as free presales for a G2 design-partner contract. Do not present it as a paid standalone product until ≥3 buyers have named a budget line.

target_claim_or_section: ER-2 revenue_per_customer $25k/$50k/$100k; 2/4/8 customers a year; T2-T3 'paid and credited against implementation'
challenge: The $50k base price has no comparator. The anchor cited (Ren's ~$50k program set-up) is a full implementation price, not an assessment price. Nonprofit selection and data-assessment consulting is quoted at a few thousand dollars per project. Receiving vendors bundle free migration or PoCs (CLM-021; the DonorPerfect/DataBank offers). Crediting the fee against an implementation Unbound cannot deliver before G2 is not a credit. Because CLM-028 already says ER-2 is never cash-positive, 08 and 16 calling it 'paid' mainly lends credibility to the go-to-market framing.
evidence: entry-routes.csv ER-2 basis column ('Ren set-up ~$50k anchor; Foundant free PoC precedent caps price'); trackD row 'Free or guaranteed migration as acquisition offer'; general nonprofit consulting guidance: selection projects from $2k-5k, data migration about $1k per database (headstart.gov 'working with technology consultants'); Tech Impact sells software selection to community foundations (techimpact.org).
proposed_change: Run a G0 price test before keeping 'paid'. Model ER-2 at a $5k-15k base with 0 revenue as a sensitivity. State plainly that the assessment is CAC, and add its cost to the CAC line ($125k ASSUMPTION in 20) rather than counting it as revenue.

target_claim_or_section: §3 items 4-5: local structural profile plus synthetic rehearsal 'exercises adapter, mapping and reconciliation end to end and yields a readiness report' with no data leaving the sponsor
challenge: Synthetic data generated from a schema and k-suppressed marginals can only reproduce defects you already modelled. Conversion cost is driven by joint, record-level defects: duplicate persons, orphaned grants, misapplied contributions, free-text restrictions, successor errors. Marginal distributions hide all of these. A synthetic rehearsal will tie out by construction, so it shows only that the adapter parses the layout. Calling its output a 'readiness report' invites false GREENs in exactly the area (data quality) that 20 says moves cost 1.5-2x.
evidence: 13 §2 T1 'Cannot answer: record-level matching, duplicate persons'; 20 R7: data quality moves onboarding from $590k to $1.12M at 10k accounts; 20 §4 'Unprofiled data plus a fixed price' = uneconomic.
proposed_change: Rename the synthetic output a 'parser/layout conformance check'. Forbid any data-quality RAG status or fixed-price quote derived from T0-T1 or synthetic runs. Require T2/T3 (DPA in place) before any effort or price commitment, which in practice means after an LOI.

target_claim_or_section: T1 profiler 'run by the sponsor' on its desktop under NDA only; 'no personal data leaves'
challenge: The tool is a vendor-supplied executable that ingests donor PII, run before any contract exists. Sponsor IT and security (often outsourced at small foundations) will require a vendor security review or questionnaire before installation. Many will refuse it outright. The T1 output also contains control totals per fund bucket and date ranges. For sparse, high-value DAF books, k=10 on contributor count does not stop a single large fund's balance from being singled out. 13 itself makes this point about amounts as quasi-identifiers. Saying 'NDA only' understates both the security-review and privacy friction.
evidence: 13 §2 T1 artefacts include 'control totals per fund bucket'; 13 'Why tokenization is not anonymization' ($2.4m contribution identifies the donor); 13 open question: 'Sponsor appetite for running an on-premises profiler (HYPOTHESIS)'.
proposed_change: Add a T1 variant that needs no installation (spreadsheet or template reports that the sponsor fills in). Apply dominance (p%) suppression to monetary cells as well as k-count. Budget a 2-6 week sponsor security review into the pre-contract timeline. Measure the share of prospects that refuse.

target_claim_or_section: XRI-013 / 08 §4: 'second migration from same source costs far less'; adapters per named incumbent report are reusable
challenge: Reuse assumes stable report layouts. Hosted incumbents ship report and UI changes on their own release cadence and owe the sponsor no notice. Gusto's parsers carry 'beta' labels and break on masked fields. NPact is consolidating FIMS and DonorCentral, which is precisely the kind of vendor change that rewrites report layouts. The prospect pipeline is sparse: about 4 customers a year, and 1 of 26 national sponsors left Ren in 2023-26. Between two migrations from the same source, the report version may well change, and adapter maintenance per source per release is unbudgeted. In core banking, reuse works because the deconversion file is a stable vendor-supplied format, not a UI report.
evidence: trackD row 'Competitor-report import adapters' (masked fields do not import; Paychex beta); SRC-028 NPact acquisition of FIMS/DonorCentral; 16 §1 CLM-015 (1 of 26 left Ren); ER-2 customers_per_year base 4; SafeAmerica needed the incumbent to install a deconversion program and supply file layouts (American Banker).
proposed_change: Version adapters by report version. Add an adapter-drift test that runs on every new sample and an annual maintenance cost per supported source. Do not claim the second-migration discount until two migrations from the same source and report version have been measured. Track elapsed time between same-source deals.

target_claim_or_section: Gusto-style adapters 'work without incumbent cooperation' because they consume reports the sponsor can already download
challenge: Self-service standard reports are summaries designed for operations: fund balances, statements, grant listings over a date range. They rarely carry immutable transaction IDs, reversal and void chains, fee accrual detail, unit history, or audit trails, all of which full-history per-fund reconciliation needs. NPact makes a full export a paid Professional Service and deletes data 10 business days after hosting ends. Ren gives 15 days' access. The cooperation-free path therefore yields roughly BalancesOnly plus listings. Full history, the main promise of HYP-003, still depends on the incumbent's paid, unscheduled PS export.
evidence: 13 §2a incumbent table (NPact paid PS, 10-day deletion; Ren 15 days; TIFIN download barred; Foundant 'as stored'); 13 §2a 'Week 4-12: timing incumbent-dependent, no public SLA'; core conversions: unclear how quickly the incumbent delivers deconversion programs after notice (American Banker, SafeAmerica).
proposed_change: State that report adapters support only T1 and balances-level conversion. Make full history conditional on a contracted incumbent export, and schedule a contractual export request at notice date. Put 'incumbent export not delivered' on the exclusions list for any outcome commitment.

target_claim_or_section: Rehearsals $8k-$20k total (3 runs, 40 h each at 1k scale; $20k at 1M accounts); time to production assumes 3 rehearsals x 2 weeks
challenge: In practice each mock conversion includes a fresh extract, the load, a full reconciliation, triage of every break, sponsor controller review and sign-off, and fixes to rerun. On a 1M-account, roughly 95M-transaction book a single mock is weeks of multi-person work, not under $7k. The rehearsals also depend on the extract: where only one paid extract is affordable (15 §1a), mocks 2-3 reuse stale data, and the final delta extract taken at cutover is never rehearsed. Three rehearsals is optimistic for a first-of-source conversion: practitioner guidance is 'at least two', and failed mocks add more.
evidence: 20 R5 onb_rehearsals $7,854 (1k) to $20k (1M); 20 ADVB-05 row '3 runs, 40 h each at 1k scale'; 15 §1a single-extract path; trackD row on mocks ('at least two'; Vibrant 2 mocks; reconversion mocks Sep and Nov).
proposed_change: Scale rehearsal cost with volume and exception count, not as a near-fixed line. Include the cost of each paid incumbent extract per mock. Add a mandatory delta-extract rehearsal. Model 3-5 mocks for a first-of-source conversion, and add a probability that a failed mock slips go-live past the contract end.

target_claim_or_section: Freeze ≤3 business days (target 2) and Unbound-side commitment
challenge: The final cutover extract has to come from the incumbent inside the freeze. When export is a paid PS order with no SLA, a 2-3 day freeze needs the incumbent to deliver a final extract on a set date and day. Nothing obliges it to do so, and core-conversion practice treats alignment of deconversion dates with the incumbent as a critical dependency. A 1M-account full-history load plus 100% per-fund tie-out and sign-off within 48-72 hours is also untested here. If the extract slips, either the freeze extends, breaching the public promise, or the cutover moves past the incumbent's data-deletion date.
evidence: 17 parameter table: freeze max 3 business days; 13 §2a NPact 10-business-day deletion and Ren 15-day access; CUInsight: aligning deconversion and data-file delivery dates with the new provider is critical; American Banker: uncertainty over how quickly the incumbent delivers deconversion programs.
proposed_change: Make the freeze target conditional on an incumbent extract SLA, or on a sponsor-controlled direct database extract. Publish the freeze as 'N business days after receipt of a conforming final extract'. Negotiate post-termination access extensions in the Extraction Plan, and rehearse the timed final extract.

target_claim_or_section: XRI-011 published migration SLA and outcome commitments (maturity level 4); 16 §5 'measured freeze ... published exit price'
challenge: A pre-revenue startup that publishes outcome commitments on full-history fund-level reconciliation is taking on uncapped liability against inputs it does not control: incumbent extracts, sponsor cleansing, and the sponsor's own decisions. Stripe can offer a 10-day SLA because its exclusions are narrow and it has a balance sheet. Unbound has $0.7-1.2M at G1. One failed migration of a donor-facing financial book (FFTC's $654.5k abandoned implementation) would consume the reserve and the reference base. Errors and omissions insurers will price in the commitment, and the 10% failure reserve in 20 was not sized for SLA credits or damages.
evidence: 20 ADVB-05: failure reserve 10% of direct cost; FFTC $654.5k abandoned implementation; 16 §2 G1 capital $0.7-1.2M; trackD Stripe row: SLA starts on valid data, broad exclusions, export timing 'days to months' excluded.
proposed_change: Limit commitments to process SLAs (Unbound's own turnaround after a conforming extract) with fee-credit-only remedies and a liability cap at fees paid. Exclude incumbent and sponsor dependencies. Get an E&O insurance quote before publishing. Defer outcome commitments until level-4 metrics exist from ≥3 measured migrations.

target_claim_or_section: §5 maturity model levels 0-5; 'claim a level only from measured data'; XRI-009 adopts it as Transitus targets
challenge: The levels mix binary practices (≥2 mocks, published exclusions) with thresholds that have no stated measurement protocol or denominator: '>50% of migrations need no engineering change', 'exceptions per 1k', 'post-go-live defects per 1k funds'. At 2-4 migrations a year, a percentage such as >50% takes years to mean anything, and no incumbent reports enough to be placed on the scale (CLM-020). Exemplars are assigned by anecdote, for example 'typical CU core conversion' = level 1 and 'many FIMS replacements' = level 0. The model cannot be used comparatively, and it only becomes self-assessable after many measured runs.
evidence: 08 §5 table and 'Incumbents publish nothing that places them on this scale (CLM-020)'; ER-2 customers_per_year base 4; trackD-notes lines 165-167 exemplars.
proposed_change: Define each metric (numerator, denominator, time window, minimum n before a level is claimed). Drop the exemplar column or mark it ILLUSTRATIVE. Treat the model as an internal roadmap, not a sales or competitive claim, until n≥5 measured migrations.

target_claim_or_section: Sponsor hours 584 (1k) to 934 (10k) to 9,016 (1M); sponsor cleansing as 'data clean-up' line; history gaps 'documented, not invented'
challenge: 934 sponsor hours for a 10k-fund full-history conversion is about 0.5 FTE for 8 months. The case cited in 10 (Hartford: 4 months of clean-up plus 2 months of dual run) and conversion experience suggest cleansing, restriction-class confirmation, stratified sample attestation, every rehearsal's sign-off, and donor and advisor communication will need several people at peak. Peak load also collides with year-end, because contract ends cluster at fiscal or calendar year. History gaps are 'disclosed' but cost nothing in the model, yet reconstructing pre-incumbent history from paper or PDF statements for donor-facing views is where conversion projects overrun (the FIMS replacement planned at 18 months ran past 2 years).
evidence: 20 R17 onb_sponsor_hours; 20 §3 Hartford case; 13 §6a duty list (8 sponsor duties); 13 §1 MIG-025 (18 months planned → >2 years); 17 calendar constraint (no freeze Dec 15-Jan 5).
proposed_change: Model sponsor effort bottom-up from the 13 §6a duty list x exception counts x rehearsal count, with a peak-FTE constraint. Add an explicit history-reconstruction cost line, or a 'HistoryIncomplete accepted' decision with donor-communication cost. Validate against ≥3 sponsor timesheets (CNV-EVB-002).
